chunks: And he, peace be upon him, said:
A Muslim man continues to be recorded as a doer of good so long as he remains silent; then when he speaks, he is recorded either as a doer of good or as a doer of evil.

key_terms.الرَّجُلُ الْمُسْلِمُ: the Muslim man, meaning the believer whose conduct is morally accountable
key_terms.مُحْسِنًا: recorded as one who does good
key_terms.مُسِيئًا: recorded as one who does evil

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about silence and speaking in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the ethical value of silence and the moral weight of speech. A Muslim is counted among the doers of good while refraining from harmful speech, but once he speaks, his words are judged as either good or evil.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5842 - The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said:
"A Muslim man continues to be recorded as a doer of good as long as he remains silent. But when he speaks, he is recorded either as a doer of good or a doer of evil."
